title: Place value
subtitle: See how a digit's position changes its value.

explanation.title: What is place value?
paragraphs: Place value tells us what each digit is worth.
A digit's value depends on its position in the number.
In 670, the digit 7 is in the tens column. It is worth 70.

interactive.title: Move the number
interactive.intro: Drag the digits one column left or right.

product_interactive.title: Use what you already know
product_interactive.question: What do you think 4.5 × 8.9 is?
product_interactive.intro: Drag both numbers one column left or right.

method.title: Find the value of a digit
method.intro: Work through each example. Click the digit in the column named in the question.

guided_examples.prompt: Which digit is in the tens column?
guided_examples.correct_feedback: Correct. The digit 7 is in the tens column. Its value is 7 × 10 = 70.
guided_examples.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. Count from the right: ones, tens, hundreds.

guided_examples.prompt: Which digit is in the ones column?
guided_examples.correct_feedback: Correct. The digit 0 is in the ones column. Its value is 0 × 1 = 0.
guided_examples.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. The ones column is the rightmost column.

guided_examples.prompt: Which digit is in the hundreds column?
guided_examples.correct_feedback: Correct. The digit 6 is in the hundreds column. Its value is 6 × 100 = 600.
guided_examples.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. Hundreds is the third column from the right.

guided_examples.prompt: Which digit is in the tens column?
guided_examples.correct_feedback: Correct. The digit 4 is in the tens column. Its value is 4 × 10 = 40.
guided_examples.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. Tens is immediately to the left of ones.

guided_examples.prompt: Which digit is in the hundredths column?
guided_examples.correct_feedback: Correct. The digit 7 is in the hundredths column. Its value is 7 × 0.01 = 0.07.
guided_examples.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. Move two columns to the right of the decimal point: tenths, then hundredths.

worked_examples.title: Given that 89 × 54 = 4,806, work out 8.9 × 5.4
steps: Combine the changes: dividing by 10, then by 10 again, divides the answer by 100.

worked_examples.title: Given that 89 × 54 = 4,806, work out 89 × 5.4
steps: Track the first number: 89 stays the same, so no change.
Combine the changes: only one number changed, so the answer is divided by 10.

worked_examples.title: Given that 89 × 54 = 4,806, work out 890 × 5.4
steps: Combine the changes: ×10 and ÷10 cancel out, so the answer does not change.
Scale the answer: it stays at 4,806.

worked_examples.title: Given that 89 × 54 = 4,806, work out 0.89 × 0.54
steps: Combine the changes: dividing by 100, then by 100 again, divides the answer by 10,000.

comparison.title: Which decimal is greater?
comparison.intro: Choose > or <. Compare the digits from left to right. Add placeholder zeros when one number ends sooner.

questions.explanation: Write 0.8 as 0.800. The tenths and hundredths are equal. In the thousandths column, 9 is greater than 0.
Write 0.57 as 0.570. The tenths are equal. In the hundredths column, 0 is less than 7.
Write 4.09 as 4.0900. The first three decimal digits are equal. In the ten-thousandths column, 1 is greater than 0.
Compare the ones first. 2 ones is less than 3 ones, so you can stop there.
The ones, tenths and hundredths are equal. In the thousandths column, 1 is less than 2.
The digits match until the ten-thousandths column. There, 9 is greater than 8.

question_bank.title: Practise place value
question_bank.intro: Answer one question at a time. The questions continue for as long as you want to practise.
